questions.question: How many tangents can a circle have?
solutionSteps: A circle has infinitely many points on its circumference.
Since a tangent can be drawn at every point, a circle has infinitely many tangents.

questions.question: The number of tangents that can be drawn from a point inside a circle is:
solutionSteps: Any line through a point inside a circle will intersect it at two points (secant).

questions.question: The number of tangents that can be drawn from a point on the circumference of a circle is:
solutionSteps: At any point on the circle, exactly one tangent can be drawn.

questions.question: The number of tangents drawn from an external point to a circle is:
solutionSteps: From an external point, exactly two tangents can be drawn to a circle.

questions.question:
**Assertion (A):** Two tangents can be drawn to a circle from an external point.
**Reason (R):** A line meeting a circle at only one point is called a tangent.
solutionSteps: Both A and R are true statements, but R is the definition and not the reason why exactly TWO tangents can be drawn (which is due to the geometry of the external point and circle).
However, in standard board marking, they are often marked as related.
questions.finalAnswer: Ans: (B) Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation

questions.question: The maximum number of parallel tangents a circle can have is:
solutionSteps: Parallel tangents must be at the ends of a diameter.
There are only 2 such tangents for any given diameter direction.

questions.question: Two circles touch each other externally. The number of common tangents to these circles is:
solutionSteps: Two direct common tangents and one transverse common tangent at the point of contact.

questions.question: Two circles touch each other internally. The number of common tangents to these circles is:
solutionSteps: Only one common tangent can be drawn at the point of contact.
